<b>Липолиз в жировой клетке.</b> Почти в: Lipolysis in a fat cell. Almost the entire volume of an adipocyte is a droplet of triacylglycerols. During fasting and stress, epinephrine and norepinephrine (and, more weakly, glucagon) bind to their receptors; via cAMP and protein kinase A, hormone-sensitive TAG lipase (light blue) is phosphorylated and switched on. The lipases cleave off the three fatty acids one by one; the fatty acids leave for the blood bound to albumin and fuel the muscles, heart and liver (but not the brain), while glycerol goes to the liver for gluconeogenesis. Turn on “Insulin” and lipolysis stops.
<b>β-Окисление в митохондрии.</b> Жирная: β-Oxidation in the mitochondrion. The fatty acid is first activated in the cytoplasm (acyl-CoA, at the cost of ATP). The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to acyl-CoA, so it is carried across by carnitine (the shuttle: carnitine acyltransferase I, translocase, carnitine acyltransferase II — lilac). In the matrix a cycle of 4 reactions repeats: oxidation (FAD) → hydration → oxidation (NAD⁺) → thiolysis. Each turn cuts 2 carbons off the chain as acetyl-CoA and yields FADH₂ and NADH. Palmitate (C16) goes through 7 turns and gives 8 acetyl-CoA. Fat oxidation also produces “metabolic water” — this is how a camel gets by.
<b>Кетоновые тела</b> — ацетоацетат, β-г: Ketone bodies — acetoacetate, β-hydroxybutyrate and acetone — are made only by the liver, when there is plenty of acetyl-CoA from fat and oxaloacetate has been used up for gluconeogenesis (fasting, a low-carbohydrate diet, diabetes). The liver itself does not use them: they travel in the blood to the brain (after 2–3 weeks of fasting they cover up to 2/3 of its needs), the heart and muscles. Acetone is exhaled — the “fruity” smell on the breath. The timescale is accelerated: watch the level rise over 40 days of fasting.
<b>Синтез жирных кислот</b> (липогенез): Fatty acid synthesis (lipogenesis) takes place in the cytoplasm of liver and adipose cells after a meal, when carbohydrates are in excess. Acetyl-CoA is exported from the mitochondrion as citrate. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (with biotin, yellow) makes malonyl-CoA — the key regulated step (activated by insulin and citrate). The multienzyme fatty acid synthase (a dimer, light blue) lengthens the chain by 2 carbons in each of 7 cycles, spending 2 NADPH (green) per cycle, up to palmitate C16. At the same time malonyl-CoA blocks the entry of fatty acids into the mitochondrion, so synthesis and oxidation never run simultaneously.
<b>Инсулин</b> (после еды) через фосфоди: Insulin (after a meal) lowers cAMP via phosphodiesterase and dephosphorylates the lipase via phosphatases — fat breakdown stops and, conversely, TAG synthesis switches on. That is why fat is “burned” only when insulin is low.
<b>Диабетический кетоацидоз.</b> Без инс: Diabetic ketoacidosis. Without insulin, fat breaks down unchecked and the liver floods the blood with ketone bodies (15–25 mmol/L and higher). These are acids, so blood pH falls; deep, labored breathing (Kussmaul breathing), the smell of acetone, vomiting and coma follow. This is an emergency: insulin and fluids are needed.
Как жир из жировой клетки превращается в: How fat from a fat cell becomes energy: lipolysis, the carnitine shuttle, the β-oxidation spiral — and the brain’s reserve “fuel” during fasting.
\n <div><h2>Энергетика</h2>\n:
Energetics

Oxidation of palmitic acid: 7 turns of β-oxidation (7 FADH₂ and 7 NADH — by the textbook, 7 × 5 = 35 ATP) and 8 acetyl-CoA (8 × 12 = 96 ATP), minus activation — about 130 ATP (≈ 106 with modern coefficients). Glycerol gives another ~22 ATP. Per gram, fat stores more than twice as much energy as carbohydrate.

Ketone bodies

Synthesis: 2 acetyl-CoA → acetoacetyl-CoA → HMG-CoA → acetoacetate → β-hydroxybutyrate (by reduction) or acetone (spontaneously). Use in tissues: acetoacetate + succinyl-CoA → acetoacetyl-CoA → 2 acetyl-CoA → Krebs cycle. The liver lacks the necessary enzyme (succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase, or thiophorase), so it only exports ketones.

Disorders

Carnitine deficiency (in premature infants, on hemodialysis) — muscle weakness, hypoglycemia. Inherited defects of acyl-CoA dehydrogenases. Obesity — lipogenesis outweighing lipolysis.

\n <div><h2>Холестерин</h2>\n:
Cholesterol

The body contains ~140 g of cholesterol. 0.3–0.5 g a day comes from food and up to 1 g is synthesized, mostly in the liver, from acetyl-CoA: acetyl-CoA → HMG-CoA → mevalonate (enzyme HMG-CoA reductase, coenzyme NADPH; feedback-inhibited by cholesterol) → isopentenyl diphosphate → squalene (C30) → lanosterol → cholesterol (C27).

Cholesterol leaves the body as bile acids (1–1.3 g/day), in feces and in sebum; ~40 mg goes to steroid hormones and ~10 mg to vitamin D.

Norms and disorders

Normal total cholesterol is about 5.2 ± 1.3 mmol/L (recommended: below 5.2), LDL below 3, HDL above 1.0 in men and 1.2 in women, TAG below 1.7. Familial hypercholesterolemia is an inherited defect of the LDL receptor: cholesterol is 2–6 times above normal, and heart attacks occur at a young age.

In the liver and adipose tissue the backbone is glycerol 3-phosphate: in adipose tissue it is made only from glucose (via dihydroxyacetone phosphate), while in the liver it can also come from glycerol (glycerol kinase). Two fatty acid residues are attached to it in turn as acyl-CoA → phosphatidic acid; a phosphatase removes the phosphate → diacylglycerol; a third acyl-CoA → triacylglycerol. The liver packs the fat into VLDL and sends it into the blood; adipose tissue stores it in a droplet. Synthesis is switched on by insulin.

\n <div><h2>Липогенез</h2>\n:
Lipogenesis

The fatty acids in fat come from food or are synthesized from acetyl-CoA (excess carbohydrate) in the liver and adipose tissue. Synthesis is switched on by insulin and excess glucose and inhibited by glucagon and epinephrine.

Obesity

Body mass index = weight (kg) / height² (m²): 18.5–25 is normal, 25–30 overweight, ≥ 30 obesity. Where the fat is stored also matters: visceral fat (around the organs) is more dangerous than subcutaneous fat. Adipose tissue is an endocrine organ: leptin tells the brain about the energy stores (in obesity there is plenty of it, but the brain becomes insensitive to it), and adiponectin increases insulin sensitivity (in obesity it is low).

Fatty liver

Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is the most common liver disease in the world; it is linked to obesity and insulin resistance.

<b>Первичная структура</b> — последовате: Primary structure is the sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds (–CO–NH–). It is encoded by a gene. Everything else depends on it: replacing a single amino acid in the β-chain of hemoglobin (glutamate → valine at position 6) causes sickle cell anemia. The hemoglobin β-chain has 146 amino acids — they run along the ribbon from the blue N-terminus to the red C-terminus.

<b>Третичная структура</b> — пространств: Tertiary structure is the three-dimensional shape of the whole chain. Hydrophobic residues hide inside and polar ones face the water; the shape is held by hydrophobic interactions, hydrogen and ionic bonds, and disulfide bridges. Inside the “pocket” sits the prosthetic group heme with its iron (balls). A single hemoglobin chain resembles muscle myoglobin.
<b>Четвертичная структура</b> — объедине: Quaternary structure is the assembly of several chains (protomers) into one protein. Hemoglobin = 2 α-chains (light blue) + 2 β-chains (pink) + 4 hemes (PDB 4HHB). The subunits influence one another: once O₂ binds to one heme, the protein takes up the next one more easily (cooperativity).

\n <div><h2>Белки</h2>\n <p>:
Proteins

Proteins are polymers of L-α-amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Functions: enzymes, transport (hemoglobin, albumin), defense (antibodies), movement (actin, myosin), structure (collagen, keratin), regulation (protein hormones), receptors.

Properties

Proteins are amphoteric polyelectrolytes; at the isoelectric point their net charge is zero and their solubility is minimal. They are precipitated by salting out (reversibly) and by heavy-metal salts (irreversibly), and separated by electrophoresis and chromatography.

Folding diseases

Misfolded proteins clump together into amyloid: Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases, prion diseases (Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease).

  • Hemoglobin — PDB 4HHB, chaperonin — 1AON, lysozyme — 1AKI.
  • The unfolded chain is a random coil with the same residues; the transition between the coil and the native form is a smooth interpolation, not a real folding pathway.
  • Amino acids are built from their formulas, without hydrogen atoms.

\n <div><h2>Азотистый баланс</h2>\n:
Nitrogen balance

The body’s proteins are constantly being renewed (~300 g a day). Nitrogen balance is the difference between the nitrogen taken in with food and the nitrogen excreted: it is positive in growing children and pregnant women, and negative in starvation, burns and severe illness. The protein requirement of an adult is about 1 g per kg of body weight.

Ammonia

NH₃ is highly toxic to the brain (it ties up α-ketoglutarate and disrupts the Krebs cycle in neurons). It is transported in safe forms: glutamine (glutamine synthetase) and alanine (the glucose–alanine cycle from muscle). In the kidneys, glutaminase releases NH₃, which leaves in the urine as ammonium salts — this is also a way to excrete acid. In cirrhosis, ammonia is not detoxified, leading to hepatic encephalopathy.

Fate of the carbon skeleton

Glucogenic amino acids yield pyruvate and Krebs cycle intermediates (from which glucose can be made); ketogenic ones (leucine, lysine) yield acetyl-CoA and ketone bodies.

Sleeping pills and sedatives (benzodiazepines, barbiturates) and alcohol enhance the action of GABA on its receptors. In infants, vitamin B6 deficiency can cause seizures because there is not enough GABA.
<b>Биогенные амины</b> получаются при <b: Biogenic amines are formed by the decarboxylation of amino acids — removal of CO₂ (gray sparks). The decarboxylase enzymes work with the coenzyme pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6, orange balls). Amines act in very small amounts as neurotransmitters and hormones. Choose a pathway.
<b>Где работают амины.</b> Мозг — дофами: Where the amines act. Brain — dopamine, serotonin, GABA, norepinephrine; pineal gland — melatonin; adrenal glands — epinephrine; mast cells of the lungs and skin — histamine; gut — serotonin. Their action is brief: amines are quickly taken back up by nerve endings and destroyed by monoamine oxidase (MAO, oxidative deamination: + H₂O₂ and NH₃) and catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT). The breakdown products are excreted in the urine, and their levels show how much amine is being produced (vanillylmandelic acid is elevated in a tumor of the adrenal gland — pheochromocytoma).
<b>Глицин, серин и одноуглеродные фрагме: Glycine, serine and one-carbon units. Serine donates its CH₂OH carbon to tetrahydrofolate (THF, the active form of vitamin B9) and becomes glycine. The resulting methylene-THF is needed to make thymidylate (without it DNA cannot be built), formyl-THF is needed for purines, and methyl-THF together with vitamin B12 converts homocysteine into methionine, which gives rise to SAM, the main methyl-group donor. Glycine itself is an inhibitory neurotransmitter of the spinal cord and a building block of heme, creatine, glutathione and collagen (every third amino acid). Toggle the deficiencies.
<b>Настроение и мотивация.</b> Дофамин —: Mood and motivation. Dopamine is the signal of “reward” and the urge to act, serotonin the signal of calm and satisfaction, norepinephrine of alertness and attention. In depression these systems are less active; antidepressants raise the concentration of amines in the synapses.
<b>Ночь.</b> Когда свет перестаёт попада: Night. When light stops reaching the retina, the pineal gland makes melatonin from serotonin, and its level rises tenfold. Melatonin tells the body “it is night now”: body temperature drops and you feel sleepy. Bright screen light in the evening suppresses its production.
<b>Стресс.</b> Симпатическая система за: Stress. Within seconds the sympathetic system releases norepinephrine and the adrenal medulla releases epinephrine: the pulse quickens, blood pressure rises, the bronchi and pupils dilate, the liver releases glucose — the “fight or flight” response.
<b>Аллергия.</b> Антиген связывается с I: Allergy. An antigen binds to IgE on mast cells, and they release histamine: itching, hives, a runny nose, bronchospasm; in severe cases, anaphylactic shock. Antihistamines help; in anaphylaxis, epinephrine is needed.
<b>Снотворные и успокаивающие</b> (бензо: Sleeping pills and sedatives (benzodiazepines) enhance the action of GABA on its receptors — the chloride channel opens more often and neurons are inhibited. Alcohol acts in a similar way, which is why combining them is dangerous.
<b>Дефицит фолиевой кислоты.</b> Не хват: Folic acid deficiency. There are not enough one-carbon units, so cells cannot synthesize DNA quickly. The fastest-dividing cells suffer most: large immature cells form in the bone marrow — megaloblastic anemia. In pregnancy, folate deficiency raises the risk of neural tube defects in the fetus, which is why folic acid is prescribed in advance.
<b>Дефицит B12</b> (например, при атрофи: B12 deficiency (for example, in gastric atrophy, when Castle’s intrinsic factor is missing). Methyl-THF cannot hand over its methyl group, so folate gets “stuck” in this form (the methylfolate trap) and the other forms of THF run out → the same megaloblastic anemia; homocysteine builds up. In addition, B12 is needed for myelin, so neurological disorders are possible.
<b>Метотрексат</b> похож на фолат и проч: Methotrexate resembles folate and tightly blocks dihydrofolate reductase: DHF is not reduced to THF, and the synthesis of thymidylate and purines stops. Rapidly dividing tumor cells die — it is an anticancer drug; in low doses it treats rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis. Trimethoprim (acting on bacterial DHFR) and sulfonamides (bacteria make their own folate) work in a similar way.
<b>Ингибиторы МАО</b> (старые антидепрес: MAO inhibitors (older antidepressants) slow the breakdown of amines, so more of them remain in the synapses (red halos). The danger: tyramine from cheese, wine and smoked foods is not broken down either and triggers a sharp release of norepinephrine — a hypertensive crisis (the “cheese reaction”).
<b>Без витамина B6</b> (пиридоксальфосфа: Without vitamin B6 (pyridoxal phosphate), decarboxylases and transaminases do not work: the synthesis of GABA, serotonin and dopamine falls. B6 deficiency occurs during tuberculosis treatment with isoniazid and in people who abuse alcohol.
Отщепив всего одну молекулу CO₂, клетка: By removing just one molecule of CO₂, a cell turns an ordinary amino acid into a powerful signal: histamine, serotonin, dopamine, epinephrine, GABA.
\n <div><h2>Декарбоксилирование</h2:
Decarboxylation

Removal of an amino acid’s carboxyl group as CO₂. The coenzyme is pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6). The products are biogenic amines: neurotransmitters, hormones, regulators.

Inactivation of amines

MAO (on the outer mitochondrial membrane) oxidizes amines to aldehydes, releasing NH₃ and H₂O₂; the aldehydes are then oxidized to acids. COMT methylates catecholamines. Histamine is inactivated by methylation and by diamine oxidase.

One-carbon units

THF carries methyl (−CH₃), methylene (−CH₂−), methenyl (−CH=) and formyl (−CHO) groups. Their sources are serine, glycine, histidine and formate.

<b>Двойная спираль ДНК</b> (Уотсон и Кри: The DNA double helix (Watson and Crick, 1953). This is the real structure of the Drew–Dickerson dodecamer (PDB 1BNA, sequence CGCGAATTCGCG): each ball is an atom. Two antiparallel strands (5′→3′ and 3′→5′) are built of nucleotides: the sugar deoxyribose + phosphate form the backbone (● phosphorus on the outside), while the nitrogenous bases point inward and are joined by hydrogen bonds (light blue dashes): A=T — two bonds, G≡C — three. That is why G-C-rich regions are more stable. Chargaff’s rules: A = T, G = C. One turn of the helix is 10 base pairs, 3.4 nm; you can see the major and minor grooves, where regulatory proteins bind.
<b>Репликация</b> — удвоение ДНК перед д: Replication is the copying of DNA before cell division, and it is semiconservative: each new molecule contains one old strand and one new one. Topoisomerase (lilac) relieves the twisting strain ahead, helicase (yellow ring) unwinds the helix, and SSB proteins hold the single strands apart. DNA polymerase can only extend an existing strand and only in the 5′→3′ direction, so primase (red) lays down RNA primers. The leading strand is synthesized continuously, the lagging strand in pieces — Okazaki fragments (100–200 nucleotides in humans). The RNA primers are cut out (in humans by RNase H and FEN1), DNA polymerase (green) fills the gap, and DNA ligase (pink) joins the fragments. The speed is about 50 nucleotides per second at each fork, with 1 error per billion.
<b>Повреждение и репарация.</b> Ультрафи: Damage and repair. Ultraviolet light cross-links two adjacent thymines (yellow glow) into a thymine dimer — the helix bends, and copying and reading of the gene fail. Excision repair: proteins recognize the defect, a nuclease nicks the strand on both sides and removes the segment, DNA polymerase fills it in using the second, intact strand as a template, and ligase seals it. An inherited defect of this system causes xeroderma pigmentosum: a thousandfold risk of skin cancer from sunlight. Tens of thousands of DNA lesions arise in every cell each day — and nearly all of them are repaired.
Два метра ДНК в каждой клетке хранят инс: Two meters of DNA in every cell hold the instructions for the whole organism. How it is built, how it is copied before division and how it is repaired.
\n <div><h2>Нуклеиновые кислоты</h2:
Nucleic acids

DNA is a polymer of deoxyribonucleotides (A, G, C, T) that stores hereditary information in the nucleus and mitochondria. RNA is made of ribonucleotides (A, G, C, U) and is usually single-stranded: mRNA, tRNA, rRNA and regulatory RNAs.

Replication enzymes

  • Helicase, topoisomerases (the target of quinolones and some anticancer drugs), SSB.
  • Primase — RNA primers.
  • DNA polymerases (α, δ, ε in humans) — synthesis and 3′→5′ proofreading.
  • DNA ligase. At chromosome ends — telomerase.

Mutations

Point mutations (substitution, insertion or deletion of a nucleotide), frameshift mutations, chromosomal mutations. Mutagens: UV and ionizing radiation, chemicals, viruses. Repair systems: direct repair, excision repair (base and nucleotide excision) and mismatch repair.

<b>Транскрипция</b> — переписывание гена: Transcription is the copying of a gene from DNA into RNA in the nucleus. RNA polymerase II (orange), together with transcription factors, binds to the promoter (yellow zone, TATA box), unwinds about 14 base pairs and moves along the template strand 3′→5′, building RNA 5′→3′ by complementary base pairing (U instead of T). Above is the real structure of the yeast regulatory protein GAL4 on its DNA site (PDB 1D66): this is how activators recognize their target genes by the sequence in the major groove. Transcription ends at the terminator.
<b>Созревание (процессинг) мРНК</b> у эу: mRNA maturation (processing) in eukaryotes. The gene is split: coding exons (colored) alternate with introns (gray). The spliceosome (made of small nuclear RNAs and proteins) cuts out the introns as a “lariat” loop and joins the exons; in this way different mRNAs can be assembled from a single gene (alternative splicing). A cap (7-methylguanosine, lilac) is added to the 5′ end, and a poly-A tail (red) of 100–250 adenylate residues to the 3′ end. The mature mRNA leaves through the nuclear pores into the cytoplasm.
<b>Трансляция</b> на рибосоме. Сверху —: Translation on the ribosome. Above is the real large subunit (PDB 1JJ2: rRNA — pale strands, proteins — light blue; this is the archaeal 50S); below is the small one (schematic). mRNA is read in codons of 3 nucleotides starting from AUG (methionine). tRNAs (L-shaped) bring amino acids: the anticodon pairs with the codon in the A site, the ribosome (its rRNA is a ribozyme) transfers the growing chain from the P site onto the new amino acid and moves along by one codon, and the empty tRNA leaves through the E site. At the stop codon (UAA) the protein is released. Turn on an antibiotic.
Центральная догма: ДНК → РНК → белок. Ге: The central dogma: DNA → RNA → protein. A gene is copied into mRNA, the mRNA matures and travels to the ribosome, where codons are turned into amino acids.
\n <div><h2>Генетический код</h2>\n:
The genetic code

The code is triplet (a codon is 3 nucleotides), degenerate (61 sense codons for 20 amino acids), unambiguous, non-overlapping, comma-free and almost universal across all living things. AUG is the start codon (methionine); UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.

The cost of a protein

Loading an amino acid onto its tRNA by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase costs 2 high-energy bonds (ATP → AMP); entry of the tRNA into the A site and translocation cost one GTP each — about 4 high-energy bonds per peptide bond.

After translation

Proteins fold (often with the help of chaperones), are cleaved (proinsulin → insulin), phosphorylated and glycosylated, and acquire prosthetic groups and targeting signals. Gene expression is regulated at the level of transcription (operons in bacteria, transcription factors and enhancers in eukaryotes), processing, mRNA stability and translation.
